epics.title: Cloud Agent Launch & Control Plane

items.title: Extend session and run persistence for Cloud Agent runs
items.description: Add a once-written run-identity field and a managed flag to the existing run table so a launched Cloud Agent run stops counting against the generation-worker admission limit and stops being subject to the generation heartbeat/progress reaper clocks once identity is captured. Add a closed workflow classification distinguishing a pre-identity implementation run from a generation run. Add a current-run pointer and any remaining host-agnostic PR/status fields to the existing session table. No new control-plane table is introduced.
definitionOfDone: Migration adds the run-identity, managed-flag, and workflow-classification fields to the run table without altering existing generation-run behavior
Migration adds a current-run pointer and host-agnostic PR/status fields to the session table
Existing generation workflows (PRD, design doc, validation, test cases) continue to pass their existing admission and reaper tests unchanged
technicalDependencies: Existing session table and its author-scoped read/write pattern
nonFunctionalRequirements: Migration is additive and nullable so existing generation runs are unaffected
The once-written run-identity field is enforced at the data layer, not application logic alone

items.title: Implement the Cloud Agent service
items.description: Deep module owning eligibility evaluation (flag, ADO-configured project, complete project skill settings, existing Start-Development eligibility, no live run on the session), one-live-run-per-session enforcement, host-agnostic launch dispatch to whichever code host the project is configured for, and start/status/cancel operations. Delegates all durable state transitions to the existing agent run control-plane module. Execution-vendor identity and credentials stay internal to this module.
definitionOfDone: Eligibility evaluation covers flag state, ADO-configuration, skill-settings completeness, existing Start-Development eligibility, and live-run presence
Launch dispatch resolves to the correct code host (GitHub or Azure Repos) from project skill settings without any GitHub-only assumption
Start/status/cancel operations delegate durable transitions to the existing agent run control-plane module rather than a new store
Unit tests cover every eligibility combination and the one-run-per-session guard
nonFunctionalRequirements: Eligibility and one-run-per-session decisions are pure functions testable without a live Cloud Agent launch
Vendor credentials are resolved server-side only and never included in any response payload

items.title: Add vendor-neutral start/status/cancel routes
items.description: Add start, status, and cancel operations to the existing My Work API surface, gated by the same Developer-group, permission, and author-only checks already enforced on every session route today. The existing session-read response gains a current-run projection (run identifier, status, PR link if any, terminal reason if any). Start returns a conflict response while a run is non-terminal and a validation error naming the missing condition when eligibility fails.
definitionOfDone: Start, status (via session read), and cancel operations are reachable on the existing My Work API surface
Concurrent start/resume while a run is non-terminal returns a conflict response and creates no second run
Ineligible start attempts return a validation error naming the same missing condition shown in the disabled-button tooltip
Route-level tests cover author-only enforcement, eligibility rejection, and conflict handling
technicalDependencies: Existing My Work API surface and its author-only, Developer-group, permission gate
nonFunctionalRequirements: Start and cancel respond within 2 seconds at P95 (persist + enqueue or request-cancel only)
Every route re-validates author identity and eligibility server-side regardless of client-side gating

personas.name: Developer
personas.description: Members of the Developer group who own Azure DevOps-assigned work items in My Work and launch, track, cancel, and resume Cloud Agent implementation runs against them.

businessRules.rule: Exactly one live Cloud Agent run may exist per My Work session at a time; Start or Resume while a run is non-terminal is rejected rather than creating a second run.
businessRules.appliesTo: Start, Track, and Cancel Cloud Development from My Work Rows (Feature)

businessRules.rule: Start, Resume, and Cancel are limited to Developer-group members with dev-workbench:view, scoped to the session's own author; no other group or role may act on another developer's session.

Start Cloud Development is offered only when the my-work-cloud-agent flag is on, the project is Azure DevOps-configured, project skill settings (provider, repository, branch) are fully set for either supported code host, the existing Start-Development eligibility passes, and no live run exists on the session; when any condition fails, Start stays disabled with a tooltip naming the missing condition and the API rejects a direct call with the same reason.
A run that completes without a PR URL is shown as "Run finished, no PR yet," never as a generic completed/success state.
businessRules.appliesTo: Start, Track, and Cancel Cloud Development from My Work Rows (Feature)

businessRules.rule: Failing unit, e2e, or WCAG checks do not block PR creation or run completion; failures are shown next to the PR link rather than gating either outcome.
When a PR URL exists, Apex writes it onto the Azure DevOps work item and shows a host-agnostic status (none, open, or merged) that resolves the same way for GitHub and Azure Repos.
businessRules.appliesTo: ADO PR Status on My Work (Feature)

businessRules.rule: Leftover work from a finished run (failing checks, incomplete acceptance criteria, missing PR) stays recorded on the same My Work row and session; this PRD does not auto-create child Azure DevOps items or new assigned rows.
businessRules.appliesTo: Remaining Work Loop-Back to My Work (Feature)

businessRules.rule: Work-item integrate is host-agnostic: GitHub PRs include an AB# work-item mention; Azure Repos PRs use the host's native work-item link. No GitHub Issues are created and no comments are synced.

assumptionsMade: This PRD widens the accepted "Cursor Cloud Agents from My Work" architecture decision's GitHub-only code-host scope to be host-agnostic (GitHub or Azure Repos), per the interview's explicit correction; the accepted decision record itself will need a follow-up amendment to reflect Azure Repos support before this ships.

All naming — service, API, and row copy — stays vendor-neutral ("Cloud Agent"); the underlying execution vendor (Cursor or a successor) is an internal implementation detail with no public name in the product.

The webhook-based completion signal and the post-launch reconciler (vendor-side cancel confirmation, hard-timeout enforcement) referenced by the linked architecture decision are treated as already-decided infrastructure this PRD depends on but does not redesign; until that reconciler is deployed, a cancelled or timed-out row may show a terminal state in Apex without a confirmed vendor-side cancel, per the architecture decision's own accepted gap.
ADO PR status (none / open / merged) is computed by reading the git host's own pull-request state rather than building a new Azure DevOps PR-linked work-item state machine.
"Remaining issues" are represented as a structured leftover-work summary attached to the existing run and work item, not as a new work-item type or a new Azure DevOps field.
The Cloud Agent continues to use the project's existing development model and development Skill path from Project Skill Settings; no new model or Skill picker is introduced by this PRD.
No new RBAC permission key is introduced; Developer-group membership plus dev-workbench:view, scoped to the session's author, remains the complete access gate for Start, Resume, and Cancel.

implementationPhases.rationale: Establishes the Cloud Agent service, the persistence extensions on the existing session and run tables, the vendor-neutral start/status/cancel API, and the My Work row start/track/cancel/resume UX that every run-outcome capability (checks, PR status, leftover work, work-item integrate) reads data from. Nothing in Phase 2 can be built or tested without a run that this phase produces.

Each outcome feature (pre-PR checks, ADO PR status, remaining-work loop-back, work-item integrate) reads data produced by a run started in Phase 1 (PR URL, check results, terminal state) and cannot start before that run/row capability exists. The four outcome features are otherwise independent of each other's implementation and can proceed in parallel once Phase 1 ships, subject to the feature-level dependsOn already recorded within this epic.
